title: Open items from the Vegeta run · Goku 2.8.0

items.title: Pick a look while setting up a new profile
items.why: A new profile always opens as Dragon Ball, and its setup guide is whichever skin was last open. Someone setting up Encore has to find Settings → Skin afterwards.

options.label: Add a “Pick a look” step
options.desc: Right after “What do you train?”. Three cards with each skin's words and colors. Changeable later in Settings.

options.label: Copy the current profile's skin
options.desc: No new step. A profile added from Encore starts as Encore.

options.label: Leave as is
options.desc: Every new profile starts as Dragon Ball; change it in Settings.

items.title: The centre button opens a menu, not what its label says
items.why: It's labelled “Check in” (or “Train”), but tapping it opens a menu, so a check-in takes two taps.

options.label: Call it “Quick add” with a +
options.desc: Same menu, honest label. Works the same on every profile.

options.label: One tap does the label
options.desc: Tap starts the check-in (or the workout). Press and hold opens the menu, which is harder to discover.

items.title: “Hold Finish to charge it up” pops up over the workout
items.why: A quick tap on Finish shows this message at the bottom for 2½ seconds, over the Ghost line and next to the weight buttons, mid-set.

options.label: Small “Hold to finish” under the button
options.desc: Always there, so the pop-up is no longer needed.

options.label: Show the message at the top
options.desc: Same pop-up, placed under Finish, away from your thumbs.

items.title: Edit session can't add a round or an exercise
items.why: You can change reps and weights or remove a set, but a forgotten set can't be added after the workout.

options.label: Add a round and add an exercise
options.desc: Two dashed buttons under the list. “Add an exercise” opens the normal move picker.

options.label: Add a round only
options.desc: Repeat an exercise already in the session.

items.title: Names stop at 24 characters without saying so
items.why: Typing just stops. “Perf Tester Gymnast Longname” ends up as “Perf Tester Gymnast Long”.

options.label: Show “24 / 24” at the limit
options.desc: Keeps names short enough for the profile chip. The counter shows only near the limit.

options.label: Allow 40 characters
options.desc: Long names get shortened with “…” on the profile chip.

items.title: Setup's page color changes on every step
items.why: Each step gets its own bright color (yellow, orange, lilac…). On phones in dark mode, a dark scrollbar also shows on the bright page under Cancel.

options.label: Keep the colors, fix the scrollbar
options.desc: The per-step colors stay as designed in 2.2. Only the dark scrollbar goes.

options.label: One color for all of setup
options.desc: Calmer. The guide's face still changes from step to step.

items.title: Two places still use Dragon Ball words in Encore and Plain
items.why: Setup's avatar step is titled “Choose your fighter”, and the arc editor says “New arc”, “Edit arc” and “Arc name”, whatever the skin.

options.label: Use each skin's words
options.desc: Encore: “Pick your look”, “New era”. Plain: “Pick an avatar”, “New block”. Dragon Ball stays the same.

options.label: Plain words for everyone
options.desc: “Pick an avatar” and “New goal block” in every skin.

items.title: Training days per week stop at 6
items.why: The choices are 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 in setup and Settings, so someone who trains every day can't say so.

options.label: Add 7
options.desc: Adds 7 to the choices in setup and Settings.

options.label: Keep 6 and explain why
options.desc: A line under the choices: “Goku plans at least one rest day.”

items.title: “Tap the mic on your keyboard” shows on computers
items.why: The hint sits under every free-text answer, including on a laptop, where there's no keyboard mic.

options.label: Show it on phones and tablets only
options.desc: Hidden when there's no touch screen.

items.title: Strength profiles start with the Soccer pack turned on
items.why: Every Strength profile gets the “Soccer engine pack” switched on and sees it ticked in “What should the app show?”. Only Custom profiles check the sport first.

options.label: On only if you play soccer
options.desc: Off by default for Strength. Still one tap away in Settings.

items.title: Every profile gets gymnastics goal ideas
items.why: The goal suggestions are one list for everyone, so a strength profile is offered “Land my round-off back handspring” and “Full splits”.

options.label: Separate ideas for each profile type
options.desc: Strength sees strength and conditioning goals, gymnastics sees skills, Custom sees both.

items.title: Settings lists fewer time zones than setup
items.why: Setup offers 15 time zones. Settings offers 5 (New York, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, London), plus yours and the device's.

options.label: A searchable list of every time zone
options.desc: In both places. Longer list, but nobody is left out.

items.title: Fueling ratios say “per kg” when you use pounds
items.why: The gram amounts are right, but the ratio reads “1.4–2.0 g per kg a day” even with lb chosen.

options.label: Per lb when you use pounds
options.desc: “0.64–0.91 g per lb a day; about 0.11 g per lb per meal.” Per kg stays for kg users.

options.label: Show both
options.desc: “0.64–0.91 g per lb (1.4–2.0 g per kg) a day”, longer but matches the cited source.

items.title: “Dumbbell math” shows on cable and machine exercises
items.why: Any custom exercise with a weight gets “Loads are per dumbbell…”, even a cable row.

items.title: New exercise uses different groups from the move picker
items.why: New exercise offers push, pull, legs, core, power, joints (lowercase). The picker uses “Push (chest, shoulders, triceps)”, “Legs and glutes”, “Cardio”, “Mobility and stretching” and so on.

options.label: Use the picker's 7 groups and names
options.desc: A new exercise then appears under the same group you picked.

items.title: One session can add 4,000 to the power level
items.why: Training counts up to 4,000 against the number of planned days. With one planned day, one session jumps it from 469 to 4,469.

options.label: Count against at least 3 sessions a week
options.desc: One session adds about 1,333. Weeks with more planned days work as today.

items.title: A rest day shows 50% before you do anything
items.why: A planned rest day counts as training done, so a new profile shows Ki 50% with nothing logged.

options.label: Rest counts once you mark it
options.desc: Tap “Rest day” in the quick menu, and the rest half fills.

options.label: Keep 50%, but say why
options.desc: The line under Ki reads “Rest day counted · protein to go”.

items.title: Android's Back button leaves the app
items.why: Goku adds nothing to the browser's history, so Back on Android closes the app even with a sheet open or mid-workout. iPhone has no Back button, so this is Android only.

options.label: Back closes the open sheet first
options.desc: Mid-workout it asks “Leave the workout?” before going anywhere.

items.title: The app icon is the same ball for every skin
items.why: A phone sets the icon once, when the app is added to the home screen, so it can't change when a profile switches skin. Only a different icon for everyone is possible.

options.label: Design a new icon that fits every skin
options.desc: I'd bring you three icon designs to choose from in the next review.
